sentences.text: Overosaurus is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaurs named after the Cerro Overo locality where it was found.
Scientists estimated this animal to be approximately 10 meters long, making it relatively small compared to other Patagonian sauropods.
This creature was a ground-dwelling herbivore.
The sacrum of Overosaurus consists of six fused sacral vertebrae.
The genus name means 'Overo lizard' after the discovery site, while the species name honors Carlos Parada and his family for their generosity and cooperation during fieldwork.
The only known specimen of Overosaurus was recovered at the Cerro Overo locality in Patagonia, Argentina.
The Overosaurus specimen was collected in 2002 by researchers from the Museo Carmen Funes, the Museo Argentino Urquiza, and the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County.
The Overosaurus specimen is housed in the collection of the Museo Argentino Urquiza in Neuquén, Argentina.
Carlos Parada and his family found the specimen and provided logistical support and fieldwork assistance to museum staff.
The Cerro Overo locality was originally thought to be in the Anacleto Formation but is now attributed to the Bajo de la Carpa Formation.
Overosaurus was described and named by Rodolfo A. Coria, Leonardo S. Filippi, Luis M. Chiappe, Rodolfo García, and Andrea B. Arcucci in 2013.

Phylogenetic analysis places Overosaurus within the Aeolosaurini as the sister taxon to a group containing Gondwanatitan faustoi, Pitekunsaurus macayai, Aeolosaurus rionegrinus, and Aeolosaurus maximus.
Overosaurus belongs to the family Saltasauridae.
Overosaurus belongs to the tribe Aeolosaurini.
Overosaurus paradasorum lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 million years ago, in what is now South America.
Overosaurus fossils were found in the Anacleto Formation of the Neuquén Group in Patagonia, southern Argentina.
Overosaurus lived between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
